<!-- pr-reviewer: 31b8e2d24dd1ec7953afbb310a66df04ef2ce806 -->
**Needs changes before merge.**

Reviewed against #1221 (five points, files list, "Done means"), trial-merged with `origin/main` at 7580cd21.

### What looks good
- All five points are in the process text. Every quoted maintainer sentence in AGENTS.md is intact, and the start-of-session duty is marked "Superseded since 2026-11-12" with its old quote kept. There are no collateral changes to AGENTS.md: everything outside the five points (and the reflow of one line in "Outside PRs are reviewed") is unchanged and in the same order.
- The old rule's safety content survives in AGENTS.md and the skill: never rebase or force-push; "stop and report the hunk" when both sides changed the same logic; a conflict resolved by hand still gets a delta review.
- Point 4 works live. The new `review-prs` step-1 query (owner = `NeoTech`) lists 8 PRs that the old query hid, because their only marker for the current head is by another account: #1112, #1083, #1082, #1078, #1043, #1033, #991 and #972 (for example, #1112's marker for head 3359e656 is by mkinney only). #1213 has no marker at all now, so both queries list it. `PR-reviewer`, `resolve-conflicts check` and the merge-ready cleanup also filter on the author, in both reviews and comments.
- The planner is a faithful port. It gives the same plan as `plan_merge_order.py` while GitHub's `mergeable` is UNKNOWN, and the same `--delta 1131 --reviewed 05a44be7` output (NEW CODE: c6091eca merge of main, no hand edits; 2c1efae9 test commit).
- It is pure, with an injected merge oracle, and has 16 meaningful unit tests. It has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests, adds no dependency, makes no shell-specific calls, and runs only `git`/`gh`. All four files are under 400 lines.
- Error handling is clean. A PR that is not open gives `not open PRs: [1]`, a missing `gh` gives `... program not found`, and a bad flag, or `--delta` without `--reviewed`, prints the usage. Every error exits with code 2.
- The deliberate change (a child whose parent dropped out of wave 1 is deferred too) is right. The reference would merge the child and pull in the deferred parent's commits silently.
- An "evil" hand edit in a two-parent merge of main is caught: `git show --remerge-diff --name-only` lists a non-conflicting file edited by hand, and a file added in the merge. I checked both in a scratch repo.
- PROCESS_VERSION goes 30 -> 31, the body says what a fork must do, there is a `Changelog:` line, and no workflow trigger is added.

### Local results (merged with main 7580cd21)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run` | plan: xtask unit tests only |
| `cargo test -p xtask` | 71 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p xtask merge` | 16 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask merge-plan 1216 1203 1131 1136 1156` / `--delta 1131 --reviewed 05a44be7` | ran read-only; compared with the reference below |

### Requested before merge
1. **An octopus merge keeps a review it should lose** (`xtask/src/merge_plan_git.rs:305-317`, `xtask/src/merge_delta.rs:91-105`). Only `parents[1]` is checked. Git does not compute a remerge-diff for an octopus merge: it prints `warning: Skipping remerge-diff for octopus merges.` to stderr and lists no files. So a merge `main + <unreviewed branch>` with `main` as the second parent is classed "merge of main, no hand edits" -> **SAME**, and the third parent's code keeps the old review. I reproduced this in a scratch repo with git 2.45.2. The reference script has the same hole.
   Fix: a commit with more than two parents is NEW CODE (or at least never SAME/MECHANICAL). Pin it with a unit test that has a three-parent `Commit`.
2. **PRs that GitHub reports as conflicting but git merges cleanly are put in wave 1** (`xtask/src/merge_plan_git.rs:25,152-154`; `merge_plan.rs:158-165`). The port never reads `mergeable`, so it dropped the reference's `github_only` path (`plan_merge_order.py:111-114,172`).
   Live: #1131 and #1136 are `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` on GitHub with 2 merge bases (criss-cross history). Once GitHub had computed `mergeable`, the reference put #1131, #1136 and #1156 in wave 2 as `[plain refresh]`. The port lists them in **wave 1, "no refresh"**: `gh pr merge` will refuse them, and every wave-1 PR after them is simulated on a main that cannot happen.
   Fix: read `mergeable` in the `gh pr list` fields, defer a git-clean but GitHub-`CONFLICTING` PR as a plain refresh, and add a unit test.
   Also: right after a merge, GitHub reports `UNKNOWN`. My first run got `UNKNOWN`, and the reference then gave the wrong wave 1 too. Retry while `UNKNOWN`, as `resolve-conflicts` does, or flag those PRs.
3. **The draft/ready flow does not close.**
   - The problem: `review-prs/SKILL.md:126-128` (unchanged) turns our own PR back into a draft on an orange `conflicts` verdict. Every conflicting PR of ours is therefore already a draft when merge time comes.
   - The exception does not help: the new ready-flag exception (AGENTS.md "Every PR opens as a draft", the "Superseded since 2026-11-12 for one case" lines) never applies to such a PR.
   - Nothing re-flags it: no text tells the merging session to run `gh pr ready` after a SAME/MECHANICAL refresh, yet "Merging ... takes only a ready PR, never a draft".
   - The quote: the exception supersedes a quoted maintainer sentence ("Once its been flagged ready to review no more pushes should be performed") without quoting the decision that allows it.
   - Fix: either keep a `conflicts` PR ready under the new rule (it is waiting for merge time, not defective), or say that the merging session re-flags it ready after SAME/MECHANICAL. In both cases, cite the authority in the superseded note (#1221's question-dialog answer "Refresh only at merge time" and "yes to changing the repo's rules to match").
4. **Leftover text in AGENTS.md "Conflicted PRs are re-merged by their author"**: contributor mode still reads "for the author's open conflicting PRs, merge main into each branch". That tells an agent to refresh every conflicting PR, which contradicts "Refresh only at merge time" and the updated skill ("Work only on the PR the merge batch is about to merge"). Reword it to "the PR the merge batch is about to merge (or the one PR named)".

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Type:** this is a process PR with dev tooling (an xtask subcommand), not product code. The precedent for xtask work is `build(xtask)` / `build(process)` (e.g. "build(xtask): one cross-platform gate and decision collector"), which merges once reviewed with no cut. `feat(process)` would hold it to a cut and count as a minor bump. Suggest retitling to `build(process): ...`; the existing commit can stay as it is (no force-push).
- `PR-reviewer.md` step 1 and AGENTS.md "Only the owner's reviews count" use `gh repo view --json owner` without a repo. In a fork checkout that resolves to the fork's owner. Name `NeoTech/Camcraft`, as `review-prs` already does.
- `refs/merge-plan/*` and the simulated commits stay in the shared repo after every run. Either say so in the usage text (the reference's docstring does) or delete the refs at the end.
- The test helper `run` (`merge_plan_tests.rs:49`) uses `unwrap_or_default()`, which turns a planner `Err` into an empty plan. Asserting `Ok` would fail louder.
- "Overlapping issues stack" is left unchanged. Its `git merge origin/main` already happens at merge time, so it is consistent.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1cca2236b84945251fa196dc5942ed6dea0e37eb -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a re-review of the fix commit 1cca2236 on top of 31b8e2d2. I trial-merged it with `origin/main` at 37482923 (clean, no conflicts). I checked all four earlier blockers in the code and the text.

### Blockers from the last review - all fixed
1. **Octopus merge.** `merge_plan_git.rs` now treats only a two-parent merge as a possible merge of main (`[_, second]`), and `merge_delta::classify` classes any commit with more than two parents as NEW CODE. I ran the new binary live against a scratch remote, with the review at the PR's own commit:
   - an octopus `main + unreviewed branch` gives **NEW CODE** ("octopus merge (3 parents)"); the last build gave SAME here;
   - a clean merge of main gives **SAME**;
   - a merge of main with a hand edit gives **DELTA** (`a.txt`).

   Pinned by `delta_octopus_merge_of_main_is_new_code_even_with_main_second`.
2. **GitHub-only conflicts.** `mergeable` is now read through the gh list. The pure `base_state` table sends a PR that git merges cleanly but GitHub reports as CONFLICTING to wave 2 as `[plain refresh]`, with its merge-base count; it never goes to wave 1. A child of such a PR waits too. UNKNOWN is read again 6 x 5 s, then planned as git says, with a `WARNING` line above wave 1. Four tests cover this: `base_state_is_the_git_and_github_decision_table`, `github_conflict_git_does_not_see_is_a_plain_refresh_not_wave_one`, `a_child_of_a_github_only_parent_waits_too` and `unknown_mergeable_is_listed_and_still_planned_as_git_says`. No PR is in that state right now, so this path is judged by the code and the tests, not a live run.
3. **Ready/draft flow.** The same statement is now in AGENTS.md "Every PR opens as a draft", `resolve-conflicts` and `review-prs` 2b:
   - a SAME refresh is pushed without the draft round-trip;
   - a refresh with hand edits goes to draft, is pushed, and is reviewed;
   - the merging session runs `gh pr ready` right before the merge, with a comment naming the class.

   That closes the path from `conflicts` to merged: an orange PR of ours is a draft, and the merge-time flag is what makes it mergeable again. The quoted "Once its been flagged ready to review no more pushes should be performed" is intact. The exception cites the 2026-11-12 question-dialog decision "Refresh only at merge time" (#1221) and does not invent a quote.
4. **Contributor-mode text** in AGENTS.md is limited to the PR about to merge, the one PR the author names, or a PR the author is pushing a review fix to anyway. I searched AGENTS.md, both skills and `PR-reviewer.md`:
   - the only sentence left that refreshes at session start is the one marked "Superseded since 2026-11-12";
   - no sentence still sends every merge of main to a delta review.

### Also checked
- The fix commit changes only the files listed in its stat. Nothing else moved.
- Every quoted string from main's AGENTS.md is still present word for word in the PR's AGENTS.md. Lines removed against main are only inside the five points of #1221.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is 31; main's is 30.
- The title is now `build(process): ...`, and the body has `Changelog: none (...)` and ends with `Fixes #1221`.
- The owner lookup names `NeoTech/Camcraft`.
- The `refs/merge-plan/<N>` refs are deleted after a run; I checked, and none were left behind.
- The test helper returns the planner's error instead of an empty plan (`planner_error_is_returned_not_hidden`).
- The files are 135, 389, 373 and 289 lines. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests and no new dependency.

### Local results (merged with main 37482923)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p xtask` | 77 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p xtask merge` | 22 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask merge-plan --delta` on a scratch remote (octopus / clean / hand edit) | NEW CODE / SAME / DELTA, refs cleaned up |

### Notes (not blocking)
- **MECHANICAL wording.** AGENTS.md "Every PR opens as a draft" says a MECHANICAL refresh "goes back to draft first, is pushed, and is reviewed as usual". "A clean merge of main keeps its review" and `resolve-conflicts` say the merging session reads it itself and no agent runs. One clause such as "(for MECHANICAL, the merging session's own read is the review)" would remove the doubt.
- **Delta review of a draft.** After a DELTA refresh the PR is a draft. The PR-reviewer agent and `/review-prs` skip drafts, so whoever dispatches the delta review should flag the PR ready after its re-gate, under the general draft rule, or brief a reviewer that does not skip drafts. It is worth one sentence in `resolve-conflicts` check step 3.
- **Wrong command in `resolve-conflicts` check step 2.** It says `cargo xtask merge-plan --label merge-ready` "puts it in wave 2". A conflicting PR carries `conflicts`, not `merge-ready`, so it is not in that list. Name the PRs explicitly, or use `--label conflicts` together with the ready ones.
- **The decision note grew** with this round's choices (`docs/decisions/1221-merge-time-refresh.md`); fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
